stories.title: Tiny shifts in iron content tip a potential memory material between competing magnetic states
stories.desc: A team of Yale researchers has figured out what gives a magnetic material its mysterious properties, a discovery that could help boost computing memory and the field of "spintronics." Their work is published in Physical Review Letters.

stories.title: One extra quantum dot helps balance speed and stability in spin qubits
stories.desc: Quantum computers need qubits that can be controlled both quickly and reliably. Yet making semiconductor spin qubits faster often makes them more sensitive to electrical noise, creating a difficult trade-off.

stories.title: Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
stories.desc: Scientists have filmed tiny magnetic vortices called skyrmions melting out of an organized lattice for the first time, revealing new ways to manipulate these unusual structures. stories.title: Diamond defects confirm 80-year-old theory of crystal stress
stories.desc: For the first time, researchers in Japan have directly mapped several components of the stress field surrounding an atomic-scale flaw in the crystal structure of diamond. stories.title: Supercurrent enables the reading of quantum information without destroying it
stories.desc: One of the fundamental challenges of quantum computing is obtaining information from a quantum bit, or qubit. stories.title: New 3D thermal invisibility cloak makes objects disappear from infrared cameras
stories.desc: Researchers have developed a groundbreaking 3D invisibility cloak that can hide complex objects from infrared cameras while protecting them from extreme heat and cold. Instead of blocking heat, the device guides it around an object, making the object appear invisible to thermal imaging from…

stories.title: How Voting Is Like a Klein Bottle
stories.desc: A new topological model connects a centuries-old voting paradox to a surface with no distinct inside or outside. The post How Voting Is Like a Klein Bottle first appeared on Quanta Magazine

stories.title: Physicists reveal new paradigm for fiber growth in neurodegenerative diseases
stories.desc: Some proteins that are linked to neurodegenerative diseases can form both liquid droplets and amyloid fibers. But how are these two states connected, and where do the fibers grow? Leiden physicists Liru Feng and Louise Jawerth have discovered a counter-intuitive mechanism.

stories.title: Antarctica’s Only Flowering Plants Take Opposite Paths Under Experimental Warming
stories.desc: A 7-year field experiment showed Antarctica’s native grass and pearlwort reworking their internal plumbing in contrasting ways as temperatures shifted.
